The appellant/accused in Spl.S.C.No.100 of 2020 was convicted by the learned Sessions Judge,
Special Court for Exclusive Trial of Cases under POCSO Act, Thiruvannamalai by judgment dated 18.07.2023 convicting the appellant for the offence under Section 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 6 r/w. 5(1) of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 [POCSO Act] and sentenced him to undergo twenty years rigorous imprisonment and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/-, in default to undergo one year simple imprisonment and acquitted the appellant for the offence under Sections 363 and 366 of IPC.

sentences.text: Against which, the present appeal is filed.
2.In the Trial Court, P.W.1 to P.W.11 were examined, Ex.P1 to Ex.P17 marked and M.O.1 to M.O.6 marked.
On the side of the accused, no witnesses examined and no documents marked.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
3.The appellant/accused filed a petition seeking suspension of sentence along with the appeal.
Since the typed set of papers were made ready and the learned Additional Public Prosecutor had no objection for hearing the appeal, the criminal appeal itself is taken up for final hearing.
4.The case of the prosecution is that the victim girl/P.W.1 is a minor aged about 16 years studying XI Standard, residing with her grandmother at Ariyathur Village, Polur Taluk.
Her parents were residing in Chennai doing daily coolie work.
The victim girl's school is situated at Vadamadhirimangalam.
She was followed by the appellant daily when she was going to the School.
Thereafter, they became friendly and from the year 2019, they were talking with each other regularly.
On 13.04.2020 the petitioner enticed the victim, called her near the tank bund and taking advantage of the loneliness, the appellant committed penetrative sexual assault upon the victim.
The victim was shocked but she has not revealed about the incident to anyone.

Taking advantage of the fact that the victim had not revealed about the incident to anyone, again on 22.07.2020 at about https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 9.00 p.m. when the victim was near the tank bund to attend the nature's call, the appellant committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault.

Finding that his daughter had not returned home for a long time, the father of the victim girl/P.W.2 along with another Villager/P.W.4 went in search of the victim near the tank bunds where he saw the appellant lying over the victim.
On seeing the victim's father and another person, the appellant ran away from the scene of occurrence and thereafter, the victim was brought home.
Since it was a delicate issue the victim's father called his relative, a lady, to enquire about the incident and lodged a complaint with the respondent police on the next day i.e. on 23.07.2020.
Manikandan vs The State Rep.

2 5.On receipt of the complaint from the victim girl and her father, the Sub-Inspector of Police registered a case in Crime No.09/2020.
The Sub- Inspector of Police died due to illness.

Thereafter,
P.W.11 took up the investigation, visited the scene of occurrence, prepared observation mahazar and seizure mahazar and examined the witnesses present in the scene of occurrence.
On the same day at about 5.00 p.m. P.W.11 arrested the appellant/accused, recorded his confession and produced him before the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Magistrate for remand.
Thereafter, P.W.11 produced the victim before the Magistrate for recording 164 statement.
The victim girl and the appellant were subjected to detailed medical examination.
P.W.11 after collecting the medical records and examining the Doctors, filed the charge sheet before the Trial Court.

The Trial Court on examination of witnesses and marking of documents finding that the appellant had committed the offence,
convicted him as stated above.
6.The contention of the learned counsel for the appellant is that the appellant and the victim girl/P.W.1 were in love with each other and they were also moving intimately.
Since it was opposed by the parents and family members of the victim, a false case has been foisted against the appellant.
He would submit that the victim girl herself in her statement admits the relationship between them and their intention to get married and to lead a happy life.
He further submit that in this case no independent witnesses were examined.
P.W.1 is the victim girl, P.W.2 and P.W.3 are the father and mother of the victim girl.
P.W.3 admits that she was not present in the Village on the date of occurrence.
P.W.2/father of the victim girl https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis states that he along with P.W.4 went in search of his daughter/P.W.1 and found the victim girl and the appellant together.
But the evidence of P.W.4 is contrary to P.W.2.
P.W.5 and P.W.6, who are the witnesses for observation mahazar and seizure mahazar are also close relatives of P.W.2.
Apart from this, there are no other independent witnesses.

He would further submit that P.W.10/Doctor who examined the victim girl states that there is no external injury or any marks on the body of the victim except for the reason that hymen was found not intact and this might be for many other reasons.

He further submitted that the Trial Court failed to consider the admission of P.W.1 to P.W.3, namely, the victim girl and her parents that the appellant and the victim girl got married on 04.12.2022 at Kumaragiri Sri Balamurugan Thirukovil, Narikundru, Polur, Thiruvannamalai and the marriage was registered with SRO, Polur on 12.12.2022.

He would submit that after the marriage, the appellant and the victim girl were leading a happy life and now the victim girl had delivered a girl baby on 10.10.2023 at Egmore Baby Hospital, Chennai and Social Welfare Department records were produced confirming the registration of pregnancy.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

7.The learned counsel for the appellant relied upon the decision of the Apex Court and submitted that in a similar situation the Apex Court in the case of K.Dhandapani vs. State by the Inspector of Police reported in 2022 SCC Online SC 1056, considered the subsequent events and observed that the Court cannot shut its eyes to the ground reality and disturb the happy family life of the appellant and the prosecutrix.

entities.text: K.Dhandapani vs. State by the Inspector of Police reported in 2022 SCC Online SC 1056
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He would submit that the Trial Court ignored the same for the reason that the chief examination of P.W.1 to P.W.3 was held on 19.04.2021 and the cross examination was almost ten months thereafter, hence the admission of the victim girl/P.W.1 and her parents cannot be considered, which is not proper.

He further submitted that now a girl child was born to the appellant and the victim girl, the baby could not be denied the love and affection of the parents and the victim girl also needs comfort after pregnancy.
Hence, he prayed for setting aside the conviction and Manikandan vs The State Rep.

By on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145973911/
3 sentence imposed by the Trial Court.
8.The learned Additional Public Prosecutor submitted that the victim girl/P.W.1 along with her father/P.W.2 lodged a complaint to the respondent police on 23.07.2020 wherein she narrated the events as to how the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis appellant enticed her taking advantage of her minor age and how she was subjected to penetrative sexual assault by the appellant.
Further in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the victim girl confirmed the same and even in her chief examination, she corroborate her earlier statement.

He would submit that in fact in the complaint itself, the victim girl had mentioned that when her parents and Villagers approached the appellant to resolve the issue and insisted him to marry her, the appellant refused the same and thereafter only, complaint was lodged.
After registration of the case, in order to escape from the clutches of law the appellant married the victim girl.

He further submitted that P.W.2 and P.W.3, namely, the parents of the victim girl stated about the kidnap and penetrative sexual assault committed by the appellant in their chief examination and only in the cross examination, i.e. after ten months, the witnesses have made a turn around.
The Trial Court for this reason had not considered the evidence of P.W.1 to P.W.3 in total which is following the judgment of this Court.

9.Learned Additional Public Prosecutor further submit that P.W.10/Doctor who examined the victim girl issued Ex.P10 and Ex.P11 and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis opined that hymen found not intact and intercourse probably might have been possible.

Further, the victim girl is a minor aged about 16 years which is confirmed by the Radiologist as well as from the evidence of P.W.7/Headmaster, Government High School, Vadamadhirimangalam who had stated that the date of birth of the victim girl was 13.11.2004 which is not in dispute.

He would submit that the victim girl being a minor was subjected to penetrative sexual assault which is confirmed by the evidence of P.W.1, P.W.2 and P.W.10 and thus the Trial Court on the evidence and materials produced convicted the appellant for the offence under Section 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 6 r/w. 5(1) of POCSO Act and sentenced him to 20 years rigorous imprisonment.
Further, the Trial Court on the evidence had also acquitted the appellant from the charge of offences under Sections 363 and 366 IPC.

Learned Additional Public Prosecutor fairly submitted that the marriage solemnized between the appellant and the victim girl on 04.12.2022 was found to be true and the marriage certificate in Sl.No.TMR/Polur/151/2022 dated 12.12.2022 was verified and found to be genuine.

He further submit that after marriage the appellant and the victim girl were leading a happy life and recently the victim girl had also given https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis birth to a girl child on 10.10.2023.
10.Considering the submissions made and on perusal of the materials, it is not in dispute that the appellant and the victim girl had love affair, both belonged to same social background and there is no much objection now.
Earlier, P.W.2/father of the victim girl on the given situation on 22.07.2020 got infuriated, agitated and lodged a complaint against the appellant.
Thereafter, the investigation as narrated above had taken place and finally, the appellant was convicted as stated above.
What the Trial Court lost sight of is that P.W.1 to P.W.3 are the victim girl and her parents, who have clearly deposed about the subsequent marriage held between the victim girl and the appellant.
But the Trial Court has given a reason that the cross examination was done with a delay of nearly ten months and not immediate, which is not proper on the facts and circumstances of this case.
It is further informed that the victim girl had recently delivered a girl child on 10.10.2023.
Further, it is seen that Manikandan vs The State Rep.

By on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145973911/
4
the appellant is a degree holder who had completed B.E.[Defence], his brother is in Army and the appellant's wish is also to enter Army.
Since both the appellant and the victim girl were in https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis their adolescent age and due to physical and psychological development, they had indulged in the above act.
The victim had voluntarily went with the appellant and for which reason the Trial Court had acquitted the appellant for the offence under Sections 363 and 366 IPC.

The appellant is aged about 26 years now, he is in the blossom of his career, he has to find a job commensurate to his education and settle in life so that he can take care of his wife/victim girl and the new born baby.

At this stage, allowing the appellant to confinement for a prolong period of twenty years would serve no purpose and on the other hand, it would aggravate the agony and the victim girl as well as the new born baby will be denied love and affection from the husband and father.
The physical touch of the father will be denied to the new born, which cannot be recreated at any time.

11.The Apex Court in K.Dhandapani's case had considered the subsequent events and observed that the Courts cannot shut its eyes to the ground reality and disturb the happy family life of the appellant as well as the victim girl.

In this case, it is seen that the appellant and the victim got married on 04.12.2022, their marriage was registered on 12.12.2022 at SRO,
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Polur and recently they were blessed with a girl baby.

Further, In view of the same, this Court is of the view that allowing the appellant and the victim girl to continue their matrimonial life and to take care of their new born baby would be the real justice.
Further, the act of the appellant and the victim girl was due to the change of hormones and due to their innocence not knowing the seriousness and repercussion.

12.In view of the above, the conviction and sentence imposed on the appellant in Spl.S.C.No.100 of 2020 dated 18.07.2023 by the learned Sessions Judge, Special Court for Exclusive Trial of Cases under POCSO Act, Thiruvannamalai is hereby set aside.

13.This Court holds that registration of case and conviction of the appellant cannot sighted or looked against the appellant as a disqualification in applying for any examination or employment and in progression of his career.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
14.In the result
, the Criminal Appeal stands allowed.
Consequently, connected M.P. is closed.

12.In view of the above, the conviction and sentence imposed on the appellant in Spl.S.C.No.100 of 2020 dated 18.07.2023 by the learned Sessions Judge, Special Court for Exclusive Trial of Cases under POCSO Act, Thiruvannamalai is hereby set aside.
The appellant is acquitted from all the charges levelled against his and he is directed to be released forthwith, if he is not required in any other case.
13.This Court holds that registration of case and conviction of the appellant cannot sighted or looked against the appellant as a disqualification in applying for any examination or employment and in progression of his career.
14.In the result
, the Criminal Appeal stands allowed.
